description: v8_execution_runs is the existing Run entity: org-scoped, state machine (drafting..completed/failed/cancelled/expired), plan_version, goal, metadata, with a full transition audit trail in v8_run_state_transitions and a typed service layer (createRun/transition/list) in executionSpineService.ts. This is directly reusable as THE Run abstraction for E4 rather than inventing a new one.

v8_agent_work_graphs + v8_agent_branch_tasks already implement exactly the NodeRun concept E4/E9 need: a DAG-ish graph (mode: sequential/hierarchical/router_parallel) of branch tasks each with dependencies_json, status, lease_owner, lease_expires_at, attempt_count, max_attempts. multiAgentWorkManagerService.ts implements claimReadyBranchTasks (CAS lease claim with attempt increment), completeBranchTask/failBranchTask (lease release), retryBranchTask (bounded retry), and executeReadyWorkGraphBranches (orchestration loop). This is the closest thing in the codebase to a per-node run/attempt/lease/recovery primitive and should be the reused base for E9's advanced execution graph.

v8_agent_adapter_invocations + agentAdapterOrchestratorService.ts give a per-node execution-attempt ledger: idempotency_key + input_digest conflict detection, attempt_count, stale-'running' reclaim window, canonical-artifact readback digest verification on replay, and a compensation_policy/compensation_required failure path. Currently keyed by canonical_run_id + transformation_case_id. For Case Workspace this needs extending to also key by (or resolve through) a case_plan_version identifier so a node invocation is pinned to the plan version that produced it, not just the case.

v8_agent_operator_recovery_events + agentOperatorConsoleService.ts already provide a full recovery/observability console keyed by execution_run_id: surfaces failed/blocked branch tasks with a safeAction (retry_failed_branch, recover_expired_lease, cancel_graph, expire_stale_review) and records every recovery action with before/after JSON. This is directly reusable as the recovery UX/audit backbone for E4 rather than building a new one.

v8_agent_run_identities / v8_agent_run_aliases / v8_agent_run_reconciliation_events (agentCanonicalRunService.ts) give a canonical-run identity pattern that binds multiple subsystem execution ids (wave8_run, agent_plan, schedule, work_graph) to one canonical run and reconciles projected vs actual state on drift. Reusable as the pattern for Case Workspace, but v8_agent_run_identities.transformation_case_id is UNIQUE/1:1 and CanonicalRunAliasType is a closed CHECK enum -- both need adapting (new alias_type, e.g. 'case_workspace_run', and a non-transformation-case identity path) since Case Workspace is not transformation_cases.

agentResourceGovernanceService.ts (reserveAgentResource/releaseAgentResource/settleAgentResource) and agentToolExecutionGovernanceService.ts sit under the adapter dispatch path and provide idempotent resource reservation with lease + retry-detection + budget/cost tracking. Mechanically reusable for node-level tool dispatch in Case Workspace, but the governance policy (allowed tools, cost class, org scoping) is tuned for the existing V8 agent roster and would need Case-Workspace-specific tool scopes/budgets layered on.

ai_agent_plans / ai_agent_plan_steps (migration 672) plus the whole-plan lease/fencing columns added in migration 941 (execution_owner_token, execution_fencing_token, execution_lease_expires_at, execution_heartbeat_at, used throughout agentPlannerService.ts) implement a single-agent, sequential, PLAN-level lease -- coarser-grained than and superseded by the per-node branch-task lease model (v8_agent_branch_tasks: lease_owner/lease_expires_at/attempt_count/max_attempts) built later for work graphs. This subsystem is still live and should NOT be deleted -- it backs Teresa's 'Uruchom agenta z Teresy' single-agent chat feature (routes/ai/agent-plan.routes.ts, flag ff_agentPlan) -- but Case Workspace's graph-based E4/E9 execution runtime should not be built on top of it. Only its canonical_run_id column / alias_type='agent_plan' integration point (added in 20260808_v8_agent_canonical_projection_bindings.sql) is worth keeping as a cross-reference, not the plan-level lease mechanics themselves.

agentPlannerService.ts's mid-execution checkpoint pattern (releaseLeaseAtCheckpoint -> emits 'agent_checkpoint', pauses at awaiting_approval, resumable) is a genuine pause/resume-on-approval primitive worth carrying forward conceptually, but it is implemented against the plan-level lease being deprecated above. The pattern (not the code) should be re-implemented against v8_agent_branch_tasks' per-node lease instead of ai_agent_plans' per-plan lease.

CasePlanVersion binding does not exist anywhere in the codebase. The closest analogue is transformation_plans/transformation_plan_steps (EPIC-AGENT-T01, migration 20260807_agent_t01_transformation_case.sql): versioned plans (UNIQUE(transformation_case_id, version)) with steps carrying capability_status/approval_class/risk_class/execution_mode -- but it is a PLANNING-time artifact only (transformation_plan_steps.status is CHECK-locked to 'proposed', no runtime attempt/lease columns) and is hard-FK'd to transformation_case_id, not to any Case Workspace entity. E4/E9 need a genuinely new CasePlanVersion table/concept plus the join from a plan version to its v8_agent_work_graphs/v8_agent_branch_tasks (NodeRun) rows, so graph execution is pinned to an immutable plan version rather than just to a case id. The versioning shape (plan_id + version + steps) can be ADAPTed from transformation_plans; the binding itself is new.

No 'Case Workspace' tables, services, or routes exist anywhere in server/src or server/migrations today -- a repo-wide case-insensitive search for 'case workspace' / 'caseWorkspace' returns zero hits. Everything the reusable Run/NodeRun/lease/recovery machinery above is currently wired to (v8_agent_run_identities.transformation_case_id, adapter invocations' transformation_case_id) is scoped to EPIC-AGENT-T01's transformation_cases, not to any Case Workspace entity. So even though the Run/NodeRun mechanics can be reused, binding them to Case Workspace is new integration work end-to-end: new identity rows, a new alias_type, and new FK surface pointing at whatever the Case Workspace case/plan-version tables turn out to be.

`projects` table is the closest existing 'Case' entity: organization_id, name, description, goal, status, owner_id, initiative_count, assessment_count, member_count, document_count. Defined twice (000_initdb_core_tables.sql and 000_z_core_baseline.sql — reconcile before adding Case-specific columns).

Real, mounted CRUD backend for projects: full router (get/list, create, update, members, finance rollup, steering board, notification settings, AI role, regulatory mode, PMO roles) is `pmo/projects.routes.ts`, wired at `/api/projects` via Gateway.ts:224/755 through `import projectRoutes from './routes/pmo/projects.routes.js'`. Supporting services: ProjectController, projectMemberService, projectFinanceRollupService, projectRoleCanon, projectMembershipIamService are all functional and reusable as Case Core's service layer.

`server/src/routes/projects.routes.ts` is a dead phantom stub (every handler returns `{success:true, data:[]}` / `data:null`) with the identical file name to the real pmo router — it is NOT mounted anywhere (Gateway imports the pmo/ version instead), but its presence risks a future wrong-import regression. Flag for removal, do not build E1 on top of it.

Cross-entity Case scoping already exists per-entity rather than needing to be invented: tasks support `Api.getTasks({projectId})`, decisions carry `project_id` with a `LEFT JOIN projects` in the my-work decisions router, and notebook pages accept an optional `projectId` on both create and list. E1/E7 can filter existing lists by this field instead of adding new scoping plumbing.

`currentProjectId` is already threaded globally through the Zustand store (54 files reference it) — including chat-message-by-project persistence in `setCurrentProjectId`. Case Core can reuse this as the active-case pointer rather than introducing a parallel `currentCaseId`.

`MyProjects.tsx` (route `/projects`, AppView.PROJECTS, ROUTES.PROJECTS in AppRoutes.tsx:1367) is the first real, Triada-canon-compliant screen for this entity — built with StandardModuleBar+StandardTable+StandardPreview (zero bespoke chrome), and its preview panel already pulls project-scoped tasks, effective stakeholders, finance rollup, team members, and program grouping. This is the strongest existing UI substrate for Case Core's list/detail surface.
No 'Case Workspace' shell exists (searched for CaseWorkspace/CasesHub/case-scoped My Work variants — zero hits). E7's lightweight Case Workspace container itself must be newly built.

`MyWorkHub.tsx` (4727 lines) is the existing org-wide My Work module and is explicitly NOT lightweight: 9 tabs (home/ideas/notebook/inbox/calendar/tasks/decisions/manager/vault/agent), heavy sessionStorage-persisted tab/document restore state, dozens of feature flags, per-tab system prompts. Building E7 by extending this file directly would inherit its bloat and violate the density doctrine; treat it as a pattern reference only, not an extension point.

Rather than writing new task/decision/notebook lists for the Case Workspace (which would violate CLAUDE.md's list-canon rule — 'ekrany listowe WYŁĄCZNIE StandardTable/StandardModuleBar'), E7 should add a `projectId` filter prop to the existing My Work sub-view components already used inside MyWorkHub, since the backing APIs already support project scoping (see E1 finding on cross-entity scoping).

Product-naming risk: three overlapping project/case-related AppViews already exist in the menu space — AppView.PROJECTS ('/projects', stakeholder registry + finance rollup), AppView.PROJECT_INTELLIGENCE ('AI-powered project knowledge capture'), and now a prospective Case Workspace. Confirm with product before shipping E7 to avoid a fourth near-duplicate surface confusing users.

`useOpenChatWithContext` is the standardized 'Chat with entity' hook already used for initiative/task/decision/report/idea/assessment/kpi. Adding `entityType: 'project'` (or 'case') plus a `caseId`/`projectId` field on `pmoContext` (mirroring the existing `taskId`/`decisionId` fields) is a small, additive change — no new mechanism needed.

`WorkspaceContext`/`WorkspaceType` already has everything E8 needs without modification: `WorkspaceType` includes `'project'`, and `WorkspaceContext` already carries explicit `projectId`/`projectName` fields alongside `entityId`/`entityData`. Setting `type: 'project'` + `projectId` on an existing `createWorkspaceContext()` call is sufficient — this is the cleanest reuse point in the whole surface.

`chatNavigator.ts`'s NAVIGATE-action machinery (`TargetModule`, `MODULE_ROUTES`, `MODULE_KEYS`, `ENTITY_TO_DOC_TYPE`) has no case/project entry today — grep confirms no 'projects'/'case' key anywhere in these maps, so Teresa currently cannot deep-link into a Case from a NAVIGATE action. Needs one new `TargetModule` case added to each map.

The cross-module 'Chat → My Work' deep-link bus (`myWorkIntent`/`myWorkEvent` in uiSlice) is the existing bridge mechanism for Teresa-initiated navigation into a My Work tab/entity, but its `tab` union and `open.type` union don't yet include a case/project variant — small type extension needed to route Teresa into the new Case Workspace tab.

Chat action registry (`CHAT_ACTION_DEFINITIONS`) already defines the exact pattern needed for a `CREATE_PROJECT`/`CREATE_CASE` action (mirrors existing `CREATE_TASK`/`CREATE_DECISION`/`CREATE_INITIATIVE` definitions with required `title` + optional fields) — no such action exists yet; add one definition, no new registry/validation mechanism required.

Per-tab system/quick-prompt maps (`TAB_SYSTEM_PROMPTS`, `TAB_QUICK_PROMPTS` in MyWorkHub.tsx) are a reusable, low-effort pattern: once E7's Case Workspace exists as a tab/screen, add one entry to each map for a case-aware Teresa persona — no new prompt-plumbing mechanism needed.

`useConversationStore` already carries `pmoContext`/`setWorkspaceContext` state consumed end-to-end by the chat UI (ChatOverlay, UnifiedChatPanel) — no new chat state store is needed for Case-scoped conversations, only new context field values.

Strongest existing foundation for a real Capability Registry: server/src/types/toolGovernance.ts (zod-typed ToolCapability: category/riskClass/mutationType/classificationStatus/defaultApprovalMode, ConsumerToolPolicy per consumerClass, ToolInvocationRequest/Trace) + server/src/services/v8/toolGovernanceService.ts (registerTool/classifyTool/setConsumerPolicy/getEffectivePolicy/enforceConsumerPolicy, backed by real tables v8_tool_catalog, v8_consumer_tool_policies, v8_tool_invocation_log, v8_tool_invocation_traces). This is the ONE place in the repo confirmed reachable from BOTH surfaces: human UI reads it via GET /api/v8/ai-core/tools (server/src/routes/v8/ai-core.routes.ts) rendered in src/views/superadmin/components/AI/AICoreRuntimePanel.tsx; the agent path enforces it via server/src/services/v8/agentToolExecutionGovernanceService.ts:authorizeAgentToolExecution -> enforceConsumerPolicy, called from server/src/services/wave8AgentRuntimeService.ts before executeToolCall. Gaps E3 must fix, not rebuild: tool lookup is by free-text `name` string match (not a stable module/command key), there's no module-scoping field, and it currently only gates the Wave8 multi-agent runtime, not the main Teresa chat/plan path (see next finding).

The actual live agent-tool dispatcher for the primary Teresa chat/plan flow is server/src/services/ai/toolDefinitions.ts (AI_TOOLS: OpenAI function-calling format array, executeToolCall: flat switch on tool name), called from server/src/services/ai/agentPlannerService.ts, server/src/ai/actionExecutors/playbookExecutor.ts, and wave8AgentRuntimeService.ts. It is NOT gated by toolGovernanceService/v8_tool_catalog at all for the main path — mutation-pause gating instead comes from a separate hardcoded Set in server/src/services/ai/sideEffectTools.ts (SIDE_EFFECT_TOOLS), read by agentPlannerService.createPlan and planBuilderService.buildPlanFromManifest. Two independent, non-cross-referenced governance mechanisms exist for 'is this tool call safe to auto-run': the Set-based one (wired, used in production) and the typed catalog one (wired only for Wave8 agents). E3 should decide which becomes canonical and route/replace the switch-statement dispatcher through the typed registry rather than adding a third.

The concrete command 'create a task' / 'create a decision' exists in at least THREE independently-maintained implementations with no shared code: (1) server/src/routes/my-work.routes.ts POST /chat-actions (case 'create_task'/'create_decision') — the human-UI-reachable chat-action bridge, raw column-defensive INSERT; (2) server/src/ai/actionExecutors/taskExecutor.ts (TaskExecutor.execute), used only by the agent path via toolDefinitions.ts:executeCreateTask — its own header comment says it 'mirrors' implementation (1) by hand; (3) server/src/ai/actionProposalEngine.ts:executeProposedAction case 'create_task' — called out in taskExecutor.ts's own comment as the dead-ended, buggy (`datetime('now')`) legacy version. This is the opposite of a shared capability: three hand-synced copies of the same mutation. E3's registry should collapse these into one command definition invoked by both routes/my-work.routes.ts and toolDefinitions.ts.

server/src/services/cqrs/CommandBus.ts is a small, clean, generic typed Command/CommandHandler bus (Map<constructor.name, handler>, register/execute) — a legitimate reusable primitive for the 'command' half of a capability registry. It is real and used for two flows reachable from human UI REST routes: initiative creation (server/src/services/initiativeService.ts -> commandBus.execute(CreateInitiativeCommand)) and project CRUD (server/src/services/cqrs/project/projectCQRS.ts). It carries zero capability metadata (no risk class, approval mode, or schema validation on the bus itself — validation lives per-command) and is NOT reachable from the agent: the agent-side equivalent (server/src/services/v8/teresaToolOperatorService.ts:proposeInitiativeDraftOperator, called from toolDefinitions.ts) bypasses CommandBus entirely and writes through its own path. Only ~3 commands are registered (server/src/services/cqrs/registry.ts). Reusable as the dispatch primitive if paired with the ToolCapability metadata from toolGovernanceService.

server/src/services/ai/toolChainExecutor.ts is a generic DAG/chain executor (steps with dependsOn, requiresApproval gate callback, $step.X variable interpolation, parallel batches) that operates on any injected `(toolName, input) => Promise<result>` executor function — it does not itself define or own a tool list. Per the user's own memory notes it is currently dead (no production callers found by grep here either). It needs no rewrite to serve E3: once a capability-registry dispatcher exists, this can be wired in verbatim as the executor for multi-step native-module command chains instead of writing a new orchestrator.

server/src/mcp/mcpServer.ts (MCPServer.TOOLS/RESOURCES/PROMPTS, JSON-Schema inputSchema per tool, executeTool switch) is a separate, older MCP-protocol tool surface (consultify.tasks.*, consultify.initiatives.*, consultify.notifications.*, consultify.search) wired through server/src/routes/mcp.routes.ts for EXTERNAL MCP clients (Claude Desktop/Cursor via user-scoped API keys) — i.e. reachable from an external agent, not from Consultify's in-app Teresa agent, and not directly invoked by human UI (humans only configure the connection). It reimplements task/initiative CRUD yet again with raw sqlite-style `?` callback SQL, a FOURTH parallel implementation of the same operations found in finding #3. If E3 builds a real registry, this tool list should be generated from the registry rather than hand-maintained, and its SQL style flagged as inconsistent with the Postgres-parameterized ($1/$2) style used elsewhere (e.g. capabilityService.ts, toolGovernanceService.ts).

The Wave 7 governed connector runtime (server/src/services/wave7ConnectorRuntimeService.ts, types Wave7ToolKind = 'read'|'search'|'write'|'destructive', ExecuteWave7ConnectorInput with ACL/freshness/health/project-scoping) is the pattern closest in spirit to what E3 wants for native module commands, even though it targets EXTERNAL connectors, not internal modules. It is reachable from the agent via toolDefinitions.ts AI_TOOLS entries 'list_enterprise_connectors' / 'search_enterprise_connector', and from human UI via connector-management screens/routes (server/src/routes/wave7-connectors.routes.ts, server/src/routes/connectors.routes.ts). Worth copying the typed-kind + ACL + health/freshness shape for native module commands rather than the connector-specific implementation itself.

server/src/services/connectorService.ts is confirmed dead by the repo's own inline comment (T7b-3/4 audit, 2026-07-19): the live /api/connectors route uses raw SQL against a different `connectors` table and never touches this service; the DB tables its CRUD methods target (`connectors`/`org_connector_configs`) have no migration anywhere. Do not treat it as reusable connector-adapter infrastructure for E3 despite the name — it is unwired scaffolding kept only for self-consistency, per the file's own header.

Naming collision requiring caution for E3 scoping/vocabulary — at least FOUR unrelated things in this codebase are called 'capability'/'tool registry' and must not be confused with the E3 target: (1) server/src/services/capabilityService.ts + server/src/routes/capability.routes.ts + capabilityEffective.routes.ts — consultant/staff SKILL profiles (capabilities, user_capabilities, capability_requirements, capability_assignments tables) for staffing/gap-matching, nothing to do with tools/commands; (2) server/src/services/initiative/initiativeCapabilityMatrix.ts + ini005CapabilityGuard.ts — a role-derived edit-PERMISSION matrix for Initiative records (INI-04, collapsed 4 duplicated permission checks into one canonical function) — a good structural precedent to imitate ('one canonical decision point, many callers') but a different domain; (3) server/src/services/v8/toolGovernanceService.ts's v8_tool_catalog — AI agent function-calling tool governance (see finding #1); (4) server/src/services/v8/toolsOrgAdminService.ts's v8_shared_tools_registry (toolFamily/toolSubtype/catalogVisibility) — this is the catalog of CONSULTING METHODOLOGY tools/frameworks (Discovery Tools like SWOT, Porter's Five Forces; consumed by src/components/Discovery/DiscoveryToolsHub.tsx and GenericToolDocumentView.tsx), an entirely different 'tool' concept from (3) despite both being W7-* decisions and both called 'the shared registry' in their own header comments. E3 needs a distinct, unambiguous name/namespace so a fifth 'capability registry' doesn't get built that collides with these four.

StandardModuleBar confirmed at src/components/standard/StandardModuleBar.tsx (exported default + named `StandardModuleBar`, props type `StandardModuleBarProps`). It is the ONLY facade for Menu 1/2/3 chrome (breadcrumbs, tabs/pigułki, primary CTA, view-mode switcher, status filters, Menu-3 chips/bulk-bar/open-item tabs). Key props: `breadcrumbs`/`breadcrumbCta`/`breadcrumbExtra` (Menu1), `tabs`/`activeTab`/`onTabChange`/`onSearch`/`primaryCta`/`primaryCtaContent`/`viewModes`/`viewMode`/`filterControls`/`onNewItem`/`categoryButtons`/`statusFilters`/`statusDropdownContext` (Menu2), `chips`/`activeChip`/`bulk`/`openItems`/`activeItemId`/`menu3Right`/`activeFilters`/`commandRowContent` escape hatch (Menu3). It delegates internally to `ModuleNavBar` — modules must NOT build their own chrome; compose via these declarative props only. Optional `children` prop makes it also own the full page layout (flex-col + scroll area), 1:1 with legacy `ModuleHub`.

StandardTable confirmed at src/components/standard/StandardTable.tsx (exported default + named `StandardTable`, props type `StandardTableProps`). Wraps canonical `FilterableTable` and enforces the 9 MUSTs (sticky sortable header w/ column filters, hairline row separators, row-description toggle, mandatory Settings2 column popover, zero-sum resize with persistKey, 3-zone kebab via `rowMenu`/`rowActions`, left-side row selection driving Menu3 bulk mode, contextual bulk actions, empty/loading/error states). StandardPreview confirmed at src/components/standard/StandardPreview.tsx (exported default + named `StandardPreview`, props type `StandardPreviewProps`). Enforces the fixed 6-block preview order: (1) header w/ pin+Open+close via `PreviewPaneShell`, (2) meta chip card (`meta: StandardPreviewMeta` — pills/trailing/recommendation), (3) Details section w/ ⋮ Copy/Export/Download kebab and optional `properties` key-value table (renders via `ArtifactPropertiesTable`), (4) optional AI hint strip (`ai` prop), (5) mandatory Relations block (always rendered, empty-state included), (6) actions grid (`actions: {resolutions, informational, time}` rendered through `PreviewActionButton`, with `orderPreviewActionRows` forcing destructive actions to always land last regardless of which row the caller put them in). ArtifactRightPanel confirmed at src/components/standard/ArtifactRightPanel.tsx (exported default + named `ArtifactRightPanel`, props type `ArtifactRightPanelProps`). This is the shared right-panel accordion shell for all 5 SPEC-A archetypes (Canvas/Document/Record/Matrix/Deck) per ARTIFACT_ANATOMY_STANDARD.md §10.2/§11.2. Canonical section order is fixed by `ARTIFACT_PANEL_SECTION_ORDER = ['actions','properties','relations','evidence','results','comments','history']` — modules may omit sections but cannot reorder present ones. Props: `sections: ArtifactRightPanelSection[]` (id/label/icon/children/collapsible/defaultOpen/badge/isEmpty/emptyLabel), `width` (defaults to `--ntype-right-panel-width` token, 320px), `statusBar` (optional slot above sections e.g. `ArtifactApprovalStatusBar`), `className`, `ariaLabel`. Two card-class variants exported for sticky vs docked layout contexts (`ARTIFACT_PANEL_CARD_CLASS_STICKY` / `_DOCKED`). Component owns rendering (header h-11 uppercase L1 + chevron, borders, collapse behavior) — modules supply content only via `shared/PreviewPane/*` primitives inside `children`.

StandardArtifactShell (the SPEC-A composed artifact shell, not a separate primitive) confirmed at src/components/standard/StandardArtifactShell.tsx (generic function `StandardArtifactShell<const S>`, props type `StandardArtifactShellProps<S>` in ./StandardArtifactShell.types.ts). It is a thin, TYPED wrapper over `NModeShell` (src/components/shared/NModeLayout/NModeShell) that composes `ArtifactRightPanel` internally — it does not reimplement it. Key props: `karta`/`klasa` (card key/class S-or-L), `header: NModeHeaderConfig`, `primaryAction` (typed slot requiring either a config or explicit `{intentionallyNone:true, reason}`), `sections: StandardSekcjaDef[]` (left-column, aiContract required per section), `rightPanel: RightPanelSections` (keyed by the same canonical id order, each slot either content or explicit `{pominieta:true, reason}`), `properties`/`propertiesMaxColumns`, `headerActions`/`headerActionsVisible`, `aiContextActions`/`toolAIActions`, `toolbar` (mutually exclusive with headerActions per §2.4), `panelWidth`/`panelStatusBar`/`panelAriaLabel`, `buildArtifactCode`, `loading`. In dev it runs `walidujKontrakt(...)` to warn (not throw) on SPEC-N violations: reserved right-panel-only ids used in left column, duplicate section ids, class-S section-count limit, missing/unjustified AI-contract exclusions, unjustified missing primary, unjustified skipped panel sections, missing evidence section for AI-authored cards (insight/initiative), duplicate action ids across header/panel/toolbar, and toolbar+headerActions conflict. For E7/E10 work: compose through this shell (or directly through ArtifactRightPanel if not using NModeShell), passing content via its typed slots — do not rebuild the accordion or header chrome.

server/scripts/migrate.postgres.ts is the canonical Postgres migration runner. Naming convention: NNN_description.sql (3-digit zero-padded, historical producers 000-945) or YYYYMMDD_description.sql / YYYY-MM-DD_description.sql (dated, chronological, added after the numbered series froze). Runner sorts deterministically in 4 phases (Phase0 numbered by version, Phase1 dated by calendar date, Phase2 an explicit LATE_PHASE_MANIFEST allowlist, Phase3 everything else) NOT by raw filename string sort, because '2026...' < '300_...' lexicographically breaks producer/consumer ordering. It also carries a PROMOTED_LEGACY_PRODUCERS allowlist and an EARLY_VERSION_OVERRIDES map, both hand-maintained per-file with inline justification comments. --safe records a failing migration as status='skipped' and continues (exit 0) - documented root cause of missing tables on demo. db:migrate/db:migrate:strict run WITHOUT --safe (fail-closed); db:migrate:unsafe-continue passes --safe despite the name implying otherwise. Idempotent via schema_migrations(filename PK, checksum, status) + ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. E13 should EXTEND this runner rather than build a new one, and verify pending state with preflight-pending-migrations.ts (checksum-drift aware) rather than --dry-run, which has produced false results before.

THREE OTHER migration mechanisms coexist and must not be confused with migrate.postgres.ts: (1) server/scripts/migrate.ts - SQLite-first rewriter; server/scripts/rollback-migration.ts shells out to `sqlite3 server/consultinity.db .backup` and writes to a SQLite schema_migrations table, i.e. db:rollback does NOT operate on the live Postgres demo/prod DB at all. (2) server/scripts/v8-migrate.ts - separate runner scoped to the `v8` Postgres schema, driven by server/migrations/v8-manifest.json, own --dry-run/--apply/--verify/--rollback flags. (3) A fourth 'Table Platform' runner tracked via server/src/services/tablePlatform/migrationIdentity.ts against a tp_migration_history table with checksum-drift detection; server/scripts/preflight-pending-migrations.ts is its read-only release gate. E13 must pick ONE (migrate.postgres.ts is canonical per project docs) and must NOT reuse db:rollback as a real rollback path without a rewrite.

server/src/config/FeatureFlags.ts is a Zod-validated, process.env-backed, boot-time singleton (export const featureFlags = loadFeatureFlags()) - every flag a static ENABLE_* env var read once at import, default documented inline. Global only (no per-tenant targeting, no runtime toggle without redeploy) - the right layer for a build-time global kill-switch on new machinery (add ENABLE_<FEATURE>: z.boolean().default(false) + a process.env read, default OFF until accepted, per project rule 'wygląd tylko za flagą default OFF do akceptu'). Caveat: several flags (ENABLE_TERESA_MINDMAP_SEARCH, ENABLE_DECK_CONCLUSION_SLIDE) are documented as NOT actually read from this cached singleton by their real gates - call sites re-read process.env directly at call time so the schema entry is documentation-only. E13 must pick and document one of these two patterns (cached singleton vs raw-env-at-call-time) for new flags to avoid adding to this drift.

A second, DB-backed, per-organization flag mechanism exists: server/src/services/v8/featureFlagService.ts reads v8.v8_feature_flags / v8_feature_flags (organization_id, module, enabled) with a 60s in-memory TTL cache, gated globally by featureFlags.ENABLE_V8_GLOBAL, module restricted to a fixed V8_MODULES enum (chat/ai_core/multiplayer/workspace/lifecycle/pm_sync/outputs/finance/results). Non-production falls back to enabled=true when an org has zero rows; production requires explicit rows - a documented source of dev-vs-demo discrepancies. server/src/services/lineage/operationClaimService.ts + server/migrations/20260802c_mat010_operation_claims_table.sql is a mature idempotency-key/distributed-lock primitive: table artifact_lineage_operation_claims keyed UNIQUE(organization_id, operation_key), owner_token + monotonic fencing_token, bounded lease (lease_expires_at via Postgres NOW(), default 30s), atomic acquire (INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), atomic reclaim of expired leases, CAS finalize to a TERMINAL 'completed' state carrying completed_result_id (an owner-table id so retries recover without re-running the mutation), bounded-wait polling for concurrent callers, and a heartbeat/lease-renewal helper with isFenced() latch. Directly reusable for E5's durable waits/events instead of a new lock table. A near-identical, narrower pattern already guards AI agent plan execution specifically: ai_agent_plans.execution_owner_token/execution_fencing_token/execution_lease_expires_at/execution_heartbeat_at (941) plus a route-level run_idempotency_key column (942) guarding POST /run against double-submission before any background job claims execution (claimExecution() in agentPlannerService.ts). E2/E5 agent-plan-run work should extend this pair, not re-derive it.

server/src/services/lineage/artifactLineageService.ts + server/migrations/20260802_mat010_lineage_pending_events.sql is a genuine transactional-outbox pattern: artifact_lineage_pending_events (pending_id PK, org-scoped, a STABLE deterministic idempotency_key computed from kind|source_id|event_type|detail|occurred_at under a UNIQUE(organization_id, idempotency_key) index so retries converge on one row), status pending->consumed (consumed rows kept as audit trail, never deleted), attempts/last_error for retry bookkeeping, replayed later by a companion reconciliation job (artifactLineageReconciliationJob.ts). A simpler general-purpose sibling exists for notifications: notificationOutboxService.ts + notification_outbox table (PENDING/SENT/FAILED, dedupe_key), drained by a cron loop every 60s (disable via NOTIFICATION_OUTBOX_DRAIN_ENABLED=false), sequential dedupe collapse, fail-soft per-row FAILED with no auto-retry. E5 should extend one of these two outbox shapes (lineage one is more rigorous) rather than build a third.

server/migrations/672_enterprise_agent_planner.sql already defines a plan/step execution contract directly on-point for E2 'contract/plan versions': ai_agent_plans (id, organization_id, conversation_id, user_id, status planning->executing->..., total_steps, completed_steps, current_step_index, plan_json blob, result_summary/error_message, is_background, scheduled_at/started_at/completed_at) and ai_agent_plan_steps (plan_id FK, step_index, tool_name, tool_input_json, status, result_json, error_message, requires_approval/approved_by/approved_at, timing). No explicit 'contract version'/'plan schema version' column exists on either table today - versioning currently lives implicitly inside the opaque plan_json/tool_input_json blobs, so an explicit queryable contract-version concept is a genuinely NEW column/table need, not something already present. The execution-lease/fencing (941) and run-idempotency-key (942) machinery on this same table (see E5 finding) is directly reusable - E2 should build contract/plan versioning on top of this existing plan/step spine rather than a parallel table.

A separate, transactional (BEGIN/COMMIT, fail-closed not fail-open) idempotent-registration pattern exists for artifact output registration: server/src/services/v8/outputsTransactionalRegistry.ts. Contract: idempotent on (originRuntime, originRecordId) - returns the same artifactId + explicit lineage object on every call, both inserts (v8_output_artifacts + v8_artifact_origin_links) in one transaction with ROLLBACK on any error, explicitly contrasted against the live fire-and-forget registerArtifactOrigin path which can orphan one of the two rows. Smaller/narrower than the operation-claim/outbox pair (no lease, no fencing, no async reconciliation - pure request-scoped idempotent transactional insert). ADAPT this shape if E2 needs 'idempotent create-or-return' semantics for contract/plan version records rather than copying the artifact-specific schema.
